relations.myth: Bossou Ashadeh as the deified Dahomean king
relations.note: Bossou Ashadeh is identified as King Tegbesu transformed into a lwa after death.

relations.myth: The royal toxosu origin of Bossou's three horns
relations.note: Bossou is explained as a royal anomalous child spirit whose bodily protrusions became horns.
Bossou Koblamin is described as Kalfou's soldier or hired blade.

relations.myth: Bossou restrains the dangerous deified Makandal
relations.note: Bossou is said to bind or restrain the deified Makandal.
relations.source: Modern Petwo synthesis and oral lore

relations.note: A disputed reconstruction presents Bossou as another name or manifestation of Sakpata.
A speculative Kongo comparison equates Bossou with the high spirit Bazou.
A speculative reconstruction transfers Bazou's fatherhood of Lemba into the proposed Bossou complex.
Bossou offers a bowl of blood rather than wine at Damballah's wedding.
Bossou offers a bowl of blood rather than wine at Ayida Wedo's wedding.
Bossou offers blood while Jupiter beats the drum during the wedding.
Certain contemporary lists describe Madan Bossou as Bossou's wife or feminine counterpart.
Modern online lists claim Kabwatye is the child of Bossou and Madan Bossou.
